help:
Usage: ethos <command> [options]

Start:
  setup         Interactive first-run wizard (provider, model, key, channels)
  chat          Interactive chat REPL (default when no command is given)
  serve         Run the web UI + API server
  boot          Run gateway + serve in one process
  run-all       Supervise gateway and serve as child processes
  dashboard     Terminal dashboard of live agent activity
  upgrade       Upgrade the ethos CLI to the latest release

Diagnose:
  status        One-screen health summary: config, adapters, stores, pending work
  doctor        Deep health check with fixes (--fix, --check-provider)
  trace         Inspect a turn trace by id, or list recent traces
  errors        Read the local error log (~/.ethos/logs/errors.jsonl)
  logs          Show recent activity logs
  tail          Follow live observability events
  perf          Performance report over recorded turns
  why           Explain what the agent did in a turn and why
  audit         Audit trail of approvals and safety decisions
  security      Security audit of the local deployment (security audit)
  bench         Benchmark context assembly and providers
  support       Build a redacted support bundle
  request-dump  Dump the exact provider request for a turn

Agents:
  personality   List, create, show, evolve and manage personalities, and review amendments
  set           Set the default personality or the active team
  team          Start, stop and inspect agent teams
  mesh          Manage the local agent mesh registry
  skills        Install and manage skills
  plugin        Install, remove and grant plugins
  plugins       Plugin × personality attachment matrix
  commands      List plugin-registered slash commands
  evolve        Run a personality evolution cycle
  learn         Record a learning for future turns
  learning      Review and replay the learning inbox
  eval          Run evaluation suites against the agent
  claw          Clawrium playbook integration
  acp           Serve the agent over the Agent Client Protocol
  a2a           Agent-to-agent (A2A) peering and tasks
  mcp           Manage MCP servers (~/.ethos/mcp.json), serve an MCP export
  catalog       Browse the reviewed MCP, plugin and skill catalog
  process       List and manage background agent processes

Channels:
  gateway       Run the channel gateway (Telegram, Slack, Discord, email…)
  listen        Run a voice wake-word satellite
  slack         Generate a Slack app manifest
  outbox        Approve or reject queued outbound publications

Automate:
  cron          Schedule and manage recurring jobs
  batch         Run a batch of prompts non-interactively
  nightly       Run a nightly maintenance job
  digest        Produce an activity digest

Data:
  sessions      List, search, rename and delete chat sessions
  memory        Show and edit agent memory; approve pending captures
  backup        Create a state backup archive
  import        Restore state from a backup archive
  retention     Show and apply data retention policies
  archive       List and inspect archived data
  cas           Content-addressed blob store maintenance
  data          Data directory statistics
  models        List and test configured models
  migrate       Migrate model names in config and stores
  usage         Token and cost usage report

Other:
  keys          Manage the API-key rotation pool
  secrets       Manage the local secrets vault
  api-key       Manage web API keys
  fallback      Manage the provider fallback chain
  systemd-unit  Print a systemd unit for production deployment

ethos <command> --help for details

One-shot mode:
  -z, --zero <prompt>   Run a single turn and exit (non-interactive)
                        Compatible flags: --no-stream, --model, --personality, --provider
  --format text|json|stream-json
                        Output for -z (default text). stream-json: one JSON object
                        per line, ending in a result line; json: the result line only
                        Pipe input: echo "code" | ethos -z "explain this"
